title: Cash timing, unpaid invoices and deposits

sections.skill: Plan for invoice timing, deposits and overdue payments

questions.prompt: What does "Net 30" mean?

choices.text: A 30 percent discount for paying early
The customer may pay any time in the year
Payment is due 30 days after the invoice date

questions.correct_answer: Payment is due 30 days after the invoice date
questions.intro: Cash often arrives later than work is done. An INVOICE is a bill sent to a customer; "Net 30" means payment is due 30 days after the invoice date. Meanwhile, the business may have to pay for materials and its own bills. A DEPOSIT is money paid up front before work starts; it reduces risk and helps buy materials. Track unpaid invoices (accounts receivable), send reminders on the due date, and set clear terms in writing, such as a late fee if allowed where you operate.

questions.prompt: Doing chores before being paid is like what?

choices.text: Getting a deposit up front from the customer

questions.correct_answer: Working before an invoice is paid
questions.intro: Imagine doing chores all month but receiving your allowance only at the end of the next month. Meanwhile, you still need money for lunch. Businesses face the same gap: they do the work, send an invoice, and wait for payment while bills keep coming. A deposit is like getting part of the allowance before you start the chores.
